body: The constraint name `ownership_fk` suggests that it should be a FOREIGN KEY constraint rather than a CHECK constraint. In what context are you encountering the error? Are you supplying the DDL text yourself, or is it being generated for you? If the latter, please show us where it is coming from.

Warnings may be suppressed using the [python warnings filter](https://docs.python.org/3/library/warnings.html).      this is definitely a CHECK constraint since that's the DDL text being received.

@gordthompson , the regex that is failing to parse is at: https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/master/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/postgresql/base.py#L3491 and the exact string in this case that fails to match is `"CHECK (foreign_property('OWNERSHIP'::text, (ownership_id)::text))"`.

@gordthompson Yes it is a check constraint, sorry that the name i gave it is a little confusing...

@zzzeek Shouldn't the regex match the CHECK constraint?

> 
> @zzzeek Shouldn't the regex match the CHECK constraint?

yes, however at the moment, it does not, and your Q was how to disable warnings.  It's not a very critical warning.

@pipriles - I did some testing and if `foreign_property` is a user-defined function that returns a boolean value you could also avoid the warning by changing your CHECK constraint from

```sql
CONSTRAINT ... CHECK(foreign_property('OWNERSHIP', ownership_id))
```

to

```sql
CONSTRAINT ... CHECK(foreign_property('OWNERSHIP', ownership_id) = true)
```

I've also started working on a patch for this issue. Stay tuned ....

@gordthompson Thank you,

It seems it creates an extra parenthesis when there is some kind of operation:
So maybe changing this:

```python
m = re.match(r"^CHECK *\(\((.+)\)\)( NOT VALID)?$", src)
if not m:
    util.warn("Could not parse CHECK constraint text: %r" % src)
    sqltext = ""
else:
    sqltext = m.group(1)
    entry = {"name": name, "sqltext": sqltext}
```

To this 

```python
m = re.match(r"^CHECK *\((.+)\)( NOT VALID)?$", src)
if not m:
    util.warn("Could not parse CHECK constraint text: %r" % src)
    sqltext = ""
else:
    sqltext = re.sub(r'^\((.+)\)$', r'\1', m.group(1))
    entry = {"name": name, "sqltext": sqltext}
```

May fix the issue?

Also thanks for the workaround

issue.title: Improve regex parsing of CHECK constraints.
